{
  "reviews": [
    {
      "benchmark": "arc",
      "instrument_review": "Condition-native review of ARC-AGI-2 public problems, inspected official scoring software and ARC Prize verified-testing rules. The supplied passages support interpretation as performance on unfamiliar grid tasks under specified conditions. Broader reasoning interpretations and the precision of AI comparisons remain unresolved. All numbered EFPA descriptive fields and evaluative items are addressed below; grouped IDs share the stated rationale. No aggregate quality score is calculated.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "1 — Reviewer: simulated benchmark-reviewer perspective. Instrument: ARC-AGI-2; developers: ARC Prize Foundation staff and partners; report attribution: François Chollet and colleagues. Sources inspected 7 October 2026. Review date, previous review, individual developer names, publisher/distributor distinctions and original/current publication dates are not supplied. Local adaptation and its authors/publication date: not applicable.",
        "2.1 — Other: rule inference, grid reasoning, generalisation. 2.2 — Other: AI evaluation and research. 2.3 — Intended population: AI systems solving unfamiliar grid problems; no narrower eligibility population is specified. 2.4 — Intended users are not explicitly classified; researchers are mentioned as users of public materials.",
        "2.5 — One overall problem-average score; no separately established skill scales. 2.6 — Other: AI-generated output grids. 2.8 — Verified evaluations specify AI settings, spending limits and one run; other routes can differ. 2.9 — Production-based grid answers, with two attempts per new input. 2.10 — Coloured-grid stimuli; exact model-facing encoding is unspecified.",
        "2.11 — 1,000 development problems and three evaluation sets of 120; a problem can contain multiple new inputs, with their count range unspecified. 2.12.1 — Reinterpreted as individual AI-system evaluation. 2.12.2 — Verified testing is controlled by ARC Prize; human proctor categories do not map exactly. 2.13 — Software-based administration is established, but hardware/connectivity requirements are unspecified.",
        "2.15 — Public, semi-private and private sets differ in access and were matched for human difficulty; AI equivalence is not established. ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 are separate versions. 2.16 — Fixed released problem sets; no adaptive selection is described. 2.17 — Other: the evaluated AI supplies task responses, not self-reports.",
        "3.1 — Digital scoring of AI outputs. 3.2 — Exact size-and-colour match on either permitted attempt earns input credit; input credits are averaged within problems, then across problems. 3.3 — Other: proportion-based raw performance score. 3.4 — Not applicable: no standard-score transformation described. 3.5 — No differentiated AI norms supplied.",
        "5.1 — Technical report, public problems, software, marking tests, policies and dated change record. 5.2 — Public digital materials; precise publication-format inventory is not supplied. 5.3 — Supplier-required qualifications are unspecified. Public data have an Apache 2.0 licence; hidden data have additional handling rules.",
        "General description — ARC-AGI-2 asks AI systems to infer transformations from worked coloured-grid examples and generate outputs for new inputs. It provides development problems and three evaluation sets with differing access. Inspected scoring permits two attempts per input and averages exact-match input credit within each problem before averaging across problems. Verified evaluations specify settings and spending limits and use one run. The creators relate task performance to broader reasoning, but the supplied studies concern two-dimensional grids.",
        "6.1.1=2; 6.2.1=3 — The rule-inference construct and rationale for compositional, low-specialist-knowledge puzzles are clearly described; broader intelligence claims lack comparable substantiation.",
        "6.1.3 — Development is evaluated through its three child items. 6.1.3.1=2; 6.1.3.2=2; 6.1.3.3=2; 6.1.8=2 — New and previously unused puzzles, human piloting, developer review and duplicate-rule removal provide an adequate development rationale. Full quantitative selection criteria and AI-focused item analyses are unavailable.",
        "6.2.2=2; 6.2.4=2 — The passages describe development, human difficulty matching and verified administration, but do not supply complete development decisions or operational standardisation details.",
        "6.2.7=2 — Content-development evidence includes developer review and human piloting; expert counts, qualifications and formal content-agreement results are incomplete.",
        "6.2.13=2 — The supplied explanations are understandable and distinguish input credit from fully solved problems; the full documentation's language cannot be inspected.",
        "6.3.1=2; 6.3.2=2; 6.3.4=2; 6.3.7=2 — Verified conditions, exact-match scoring, interpretation limits and development/evaluation separation provide usable guidance, with unresolved operational and terminology details.",
        "6.3.8=2; 6.3.9=2; 6.3.10=2; 6.2.14=2; 6.4=2 — Software, marking tests, report references and revision records support basic use. Documentation is adequate for the described task evaluation, not a complete account of precision or broader validity.",
        "7.1.2=2; 7.1.3=2; 7.1.4=2; 7.1.7=2; 7.1.8=2 — Worked examples, a specified grid output and explicit correctness requirements support administration. Public corrections show review activity, while complete interface and material audits are absent.",
        "10.1 — Content evidence is assessed through 6.1.3.2 and 6.2.7, as EFPA directs: puzzles directly sample example-based grid-rule inference, without establishing coverage of general intelligence.",
        "10.5=2 for the narrow grid-task interpretation; 10.5=0 for broader intelligence or real-world predictive interpretations — The task-content link supports a bounded performance interpretation. No supplied external validation supports the broader claims.",
        "11.1.1=2; 11.1.2=2; 11.2=2 — Low-specialist-knowledge design, explicit development/evaluation separation and exposure controls address some comparability concerns. They do not establish equivalence across AI configurations.",
        "11.8=2 — Guidance provides basic support for fair comparison within a specified verified-testing route; differing routes and unresolved exposure and precision issues limit generalisation."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "3.2; 6.3.2; 6.3.4 — Software awards partial problem credit when only some inputs are solved, whereas dataset instructions reserve 'fully solved' for all inputs. Reporting must distinguish these quantities.",
        "7.1.7; 8.3.2.1 — A public change record documents corrected squares and unclear examples. It does not recalculate every affected AI score, so comparisons need explicit problem and code versions.",
        "9.3; 9.4 — Verified testing uses one run. Human difficulty matching of evaluation sets does not establish AI repeatability or alternate-form equivalence.",
        "10.4; 11.5 — Public evaluation problems are accessible, and hidden-data policy acknowledges possible leakage. These are exposure concerns, not evidence that a particular AI result was contaminated."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "2.7 — Under an AI-interface reinterpretation, language comprehension/fluency, reading, writing and grid-perception prerequisites have 'information missing': exact encodings and capability limits are unspecified. Other prerequisite: required output-format competence is described, but tolerated limitations are not.",
        "2.14 — Preparation, administration, scoring, analysis and feedback times are unspecified. Scoring is automated, so manual calculation time is zero; elapsed computation and operator handling time are not established.",
        "4.1 — Availability and number of digitally generated interpretive reports are unknown. 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 4.9, 4.10 — Report identity, presentation, structure, context sensitivity, development, modifiability, transparency, content and recipients are unspecified. Claimed public outputs and scores do not establish an interpretive reporting system.",
        "6.1.2=0 — The supplied rationale does not include a sufficient empirical research synthesis supporting the broader construct.",
        "6.1.5 — Psychometric framework unspecified; human difficulty informed selection, but numerical item indices, discrimination, distractor analyses and DIF results are not supplied. 6.1.6=0; 6.1.7=0 — Human sessions and difficulty matching do not provide sufficient AI item-analysis methodology or results.",
        "6.2.6=0; 6.2.8=0; 6.2.9=0; 6.2.10=0 — Documentation lacks sufficient precision analyses, dimensionality findings, external-variable validation and other formal validity studies.",
        "6.2.11=2; 6.3.6=2 — Exposure and testing-route guidance offer basic comparability information, but AI subgroup precision, invariance and bias analyses are missing.",
        "6.2.12=0; 6.3.5=0 — Interpretive-report documentation and instructions for feedback to human stakeholders are not supplied.",
        "7.1.1=0; 7.1.5=0 — Some scoring tests were inspected, but operational robustness and administrator/model interface quality were not sufficiently evaluated.",
        "8.1; 8.1.1=0; 8.1.2=0; 8.1.3; 8.1.3.1=0; 8.1.3.2=0; 8.1.3.3=0; 8.1.4 — For any population-relative interpretation, no AI reference norms, representative sample, classical/continuous norming study, modelling evidence or sampling procedure is supplied. The 407 human participants are not an AI norm sample. Norming method applicability remains unresolved.",
        "8.2; 8.2.1; 8.2.1.1=0; 8.2.1.2=0; 8.2.1.3; 8.2.1.4; 8.2.1.5=0; 8.2.2=0 — For any competence-threshold interpretation, no standard-setting judges, training, judge count, procedure, agreement method/coefficient or empirically validated cut score is supplied. Exact-match answer keys are not competence cut scores.",
        "8.3; 8.3.1=0; 8.3.2; 8.3.2.1=0; 8.3.2.2; 8.3.2.3; 8.3.3=0 — Norm dates, adequacy checks and fairness evidence are unavailable for interpretations requiring norms. No norm-based generalisation is supported; the narrow raw-performance exception is recorded under reinterpretations.",
        "9.1 — No reliability coefficient or standard-error estimate is supplied. 9.3; 9.3.1=0; 9.3.2=0; 9.3.3; 9.3.4 — No repeated-identical-test sample, coefficient, interval or matching information.",
        "9.4; 9.4.1=0; 9.4.2=0; 9.4.3 — No AI alternate-form study, coefficient or sample-matching evidence; human difficulty matching answers a different question.",
        "9.5; 9.5.1=0; 9.5.2; 9.5.3=0 — No IRT study, sample, indicator or information/precision result is supplied; use of IRT is not established.",
        "9.7; 9.7.1=0; 9.7.2; 9.7.3=0 — No other AI precision study, method, sample or result is supplied. 9.8=0 — Reliability/precision cannot be rated; one-run results and software checks do not estimate score uncertainty.",
        "10.2; 10.2.1 — No internal-structure design is reported. 10.2.2=0; 10.2.3=0 — No dimensionality or AI-group invariance/DIF evidence supports a latent reasoning interpretation.",
        "10.3; 10.3.1; 10.3.1.1 — Human background associations are described; no corresponding AI construct-validation design is supplied. 10.3.1.2=0 — The reported absence of clear human background associations is not an AI known-groups validation study.",
        "10.3.1.3=0; 10.3.1.4=0; 10.3.1.5=0; 10.3.1.6=0; 10.3.1.7=0 — No convergent, discriminant, MTMM, experimental or other AI relationship evidence is supplied; applicability of optional designs is unresolved.",
        "10.3.1.8=0; 10.3.1.9=0; 10.3.1.10; 10.3.1.11=0 — Relevant AI validation sample sizes, marker quality, study ages and sufficient relationship findings are missing. Human participant/session counts cannot substitute for these.",
        "10.3.2; 10.3.2.1 — No predictive, concurrent or postdictive external-criterion study is supplied. 10.3.2.2=0; 10.3.2.3=0; 10.3.2.4=0; 10.3.2.6; 10.3.2.7=0 — Samples, criterion quality, relationship strength and study dates are unavailable for broader real-world predictions.",
        "10.4.1 — Design efforts address unintended solution routes and exposure, but no formal response-process or consequences study is supplied. 10.4.2=0; 10.4.3=0 — Their methodological adequacy and success in excluding unintended strategies cannot be rated.",
        "11.3=0; 11.4=0; 11.5=0 — No sufficient AI subgroup piloting, equivalent precision or differential-validity evidence is supplied. Human background findings do not establish AI-system fairness.",
        "11.6; 11.6.1=0; 11.6.2=0 — Fairness of population-relative or competence-threshold interpretations cannot be established without relevant norms or standards. 11.7=0 — No interpretive-report fairness evidence is supplied.",
        "12.1=0; 12.2=0; 12.3=0; 12.4=0; 12.5=0; 12.6=0; 12.7=0 — Conditional report review: no report system or three scored profile reports are supplied, preventing assessment of scope, consistency, validity, fairness, acceptability, detail and overall adequacy. Applicability is unknown, not established as absent."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "Instrument and rating key — EFPA Test Review Model 2025, version 5.0, is retained: n/a=not applicable; 0=insufficient information; 1=inadequate; 2=adequate; 3=good; 4=excellent. A 0 is an evidence gap, not demonstrated poor performance. Section judgments use reasons, not arithmetic averages.",
        "AI mapping — Test taker means evaluated AI system/configuration; administrator means benchmark operator; response means generated output; fair use concerns comparable evaluation conditions and justified interpretations. This does not attribute human psychology or identity to an AI.",
        "2.7 — Literal human attention, handedness, hearing, motor ability, vision and digital experience: irrelevant/not necessary for this software evaluation. Grid perception is separately considered as an interface prerequisite; human reading/writing and language categories are reinterpreted as input/output capabilities.",
        "6.1.4=n/a; 6.2.3=n/a — No translated or locally adapted benchmark is described. Reinterpreting EFPA for AI is not evidence that ARC itself underwent translation/adaptation.",
        "6.2.5=n/a; 6.3.3=n/a; 8.1; 8.2; 8.3.1; 8.3.2; 8.3.2.1; 8.3.2.2; 8.3.2.3; 8.3.3=n/a for narrowly reporting/ranking observed raw grid performance — EFPA permits a justified no-norm exception for restricted raw-score uses. The supplied broader claims prevent extending this exception to population-relative or competence-standard interpretations; their missing-evidence ratings are recorded separately.",
        "6.3.5 — Human test-taker debriefing is inapplicable; stakeholder feedback remains applicable and insufficiently documented.",
        "7.1.6=n/a — Human disability accommodation does not apply to AI test takers. Relevant interface comparability is considered in sections 7 and 11. 7.2; 7.2.1; 7.2.2; 7.2.3; 7.2.4; 7.2.5; 7.2.6; 7.2.7=n/a — No paper-and-pencil administration is described.",
        "9.2; 9.2.1; 9.2.2; 9.2.3; 9.2.4=n/a for the heterogeneous task aggregate — EFPA cautions against internal consistency for heterogeneous scales; no separately established homogeneous skill scales are supplied. Appropriate alternative precision evidence remains required.",
        "9.6; 9.6.1; 9.6.2; 9.6.3=n/a — Operational exact-match scoring involves no judgemental rater. Correct answer construction and software correctness remain separate development/scoring questions.",
        "10.3.2.5=n/a — No diagnostic classification purpose is described. 11.6.1 and 11.6.2=n/a for the restricted raw-performance use, but unresolved for broader norm/threshold interpretations.",
        "Original guidance — No human sample-size threshold is mechanically applied to puzzle counts or repeated sessions. No coefficient thresholds can be applied without relevant estimates. Normative age bands cannot be scored from source-inspection dates.",
        "Final evaluation — Strengths are explicit grid scoring, public inspectability and documented development and revisions. The critical precision rating 9.8=0 and broader-validity rating 10.5=0 trigger EFPA's restriction to research or exceptional expert use for those unsupported interpretations. Exploratory grid-performance reporting is defensible; fine rankings and broad intelligence conclusions are not established.",
        "Conclusions — Users need competence in benchmark administration, scoring, version control and uncertainty interpretation; supplier qualification requirements are unknown. Ongoing corrections are documented, but no fuller future research plan is supplied. This review implies no EFPA endorsement.",
        "Summary of ratings — 6.4=2; 7.1.8=2; 7.2.7=n/a; 8.3.3=n/a for restricted raw performance and 0 for norm-dependent claims; 9.8=0; 10.5=2 for narrow task interpretation and 0 for broader claims; 11.8=2; 12.7=0 conditionally. The original summary's reference to 7.2.8 conflicts with its detailed 7.2.7; no separate 7.2.8 criteria were supplied.",
        "Part C — Sources used: supplied ARC-AGI-2 passages and supplied EFPA extraction only. EFPA attribution: European Federation of Psychologists’ Associations AISBL, 2025, Model for the Review, Description and Evaluation of Psychological and Educational Tests, https://www.efpa.eu/, CC BY-SA 4.0. The authoritative PDF was not inspected or its supplied hash independently verified. Embedded bibliography entries were not independently consulted. Omissions: none from the supplied numbered fields/items."
      ],
      "closing_note": "Unclear instructions concern 'fully solved' versus fractional problem scores, exact model-facing grid encodings and how discouraged evaluation-specific tuning is operationalised. Corrected unclear examples are documented; no unsupported claim is made that all remaining questions are clear."
    },
    {
      "benchmark": "designqa",
      "instrument_review": "Condition-native review of the original 2024 DesignQA benchmark and supplied account of public scoring software. Scores describe performance on the sampled Formula SAE tasks with the tested information-supply arrangements. Broader engineering competence, latent skill interpretations and fine rankings are not established. All numbered EFPA descriptive fields and evaluative items are addressed below; grouped IDs share the stated rationale. No aggregate quality score is calculated.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "1 — Reviewer: simulated benchmark-reviewer perspective. Instrument: DesignQA, original 2024 benchmark; creators: researchers and engineers. Sources inspected 6 October 2026. Review date, previous review, named authors, publisher/distributor distinctions and later edition dates are not supplied. Local adaptation and its authors/publication date: not applicable.",
        "2.1 — Other: rule retrieval, engineering-document interpretation, design assessment. 2.2 — Other: AI engineering-task evaluation. 2.3 — Intended population: AI systems answering engineering-document questions; narrower eligibility is unspecified. 2.4 — Intended user qualifications are not explicitly stated; researchers can inspect public materials.",
        "2.5 — Six question-group scores and an equal-weight overall score. Groups cover individual-rule retrieval, related-rule retrieval, terminology, component presence, dimensional compliance and functional performance. Their status as distinct latent skills is not established.",
        "2.6 — Other: AI-generated text/yes-no responses. 2.8 — Instructions and settings are described, but information supply differs: whole rulebook versus retrieved passages. 2.9 — Open answers and yes/no selections, sometimes with explanations. 2.10 — Text, vehicle images and drawings.",
        "2.11 — 1,451 question-answer pairs; individual-rule retrieval has 1,192 and functional performance has 16. Counts for the other four groups are not supplied here. 2.12.1 — Reinterpreted as individual AI-system evaluation. 2.12.2 — Paper evaluations describe researcher-set conditions; exact fit to human supervision categories is unspecified. 2.13 — Public software establishes digital administration; hardware/connectivity requirements are unspecified.",
        "2.15 — Passage, dimension-label, scale-bar and highlighting variants are studied, without established parallel-form status. 2.16 — Released question collection is fixed; no adaptive item selection is described. 2.17 — Other: evaluated AI systems provide task answers, not self-reports.",
        "3.1 — Digital scoring. 3.2 — Answer-text similarity and yes/no correctness, with some explanations also scored for similarity; the overall score equally weights six groups. 3.3 — Other: task-specific scores and their equal-weight composite. 3.4 — Not applicable: no standard-score transformation described. 3.5 — No differentiated norms supplied.",
        "5.1 — Paper, public questions, instructions, scoring code, small marking-test files and some AI responses. 5.2 — Public digital materials; exact publication-format inventory is unspecified. 5.3 — Required supplier qualifications are unspecified.",
        "General description — DesignQA evaluates AI responses to Formula SAE rules, vehicle images and drawings through 1,451 questions in six groups. It samples retrieval, terminology, component recognition and design-compliance tasks. Answers are assessed using text similarity and/or yes/no correctness, and public software equally weights group scores. Evaluated systems sometimes receive different information supplies. The paper acknowledges restricted document coverage and imperfect marking; generalisation to another technical document remains uncertain.",
        "6.1.1=2; 6.2.1=3 — The authors give a clear practical rationale linking questions to parts of engineering work, while the broader construct remains incompletely specified.",
        "6.1.3 — Development is evaluated through its child items. 6.1.3.2=2; 6.1.3.3=2 — Real rulebooks, designs and test data plus practitioner/researcher contributions and additional review support content development. Review exceptions and incomplete selection criteria limit confidence.",
        "6.2.2=2; 6.2.7=2 — Development and content checks are described, including two additional reviewers and exceptions; qualifications, formal agreement and residual-error estimates are incomplete.",
        "6.2.4=2; 6.2.10=2 — Instructions, settings and input-manipulation studies are described, but historical result provenance and the inferential reach of these studies are limited.",
        "6.2.13=2 — The supplied descriptions are understandable and acknowledge limitations; the complete documentation's language cannot be inspected.",
        "6.3.1=2; 6.3.2=2; 6.3.4=2; 6.3.9=2 — Instructions, scoring descriptions, discussion of known scoring limits and supporting paper/code enable basic interpretation. Complete reproduction and scoring validation are unavailable.",
        "6.2.14=2; 6.3.10=2; 6.4=2 — Documentation is adequate for understanding the sampled tasks and limitations, but does not establish score precision or broad engineering validity.",
        "7.1.2=2; 7.1.3=2; 7.1.4=2 — Public questions and instructions specify text or yes/no responses and use concrete engineering materials; complete interface checks are unavailable.",
        "10.1 — Content evidence is assessed through 6.1.3.2 and 6.2.7, as EFPA directs. Tasks connect directly to the named engineering activities, while one rulebook and limited task coverage constrain generalisation.",
        "10.3.1.1 — Other: comparisons with random guessing and other AI systems; experimental input manipulations are also described. 10.3.1.6=2 — Manipulating passages, labels, scale bars and highlighting provides useful evidence about condition sensitivity, without establishing an independent engineering-competence criterion.",
        "10.5=2 for describing task-specific operational scores under stated conditions; 10.5=0 for distinct latent skills or broader engineering competence — Real task materials support a bounded interpretation, but documented scoring confounds and absent external validation restrict stronger conclusions."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "3.2; 6.1.3.1=1; 6.1.8=1 — Equal group weighting combines very uneven groups and different marking methods without supplied validation of the composite. Documented wording/formatting penalties weaken the design as a measure of engineering understanding, though the arithmetic score remains defined.",
        "6.3.2; 10.5 — Missing commas and valid related rules absent from supplied answers can affect credit. These are documented scoring-content problems, not merely missing reliability evidence.",
        "2.8; 6.3.1; 11.1.2 — Some systems receive the whole rulebook and others retrieved passages. Comparisons therefore concern AI-plus-information-supply configurations; attributing differences solely to the underlying AI is unsupported.",
        "2.11; 7.1.7=1; 7.1.8=1 — A released answer file has fewer rows than the paper's corresponding question count. This is a material completeness problem in the inspected release; the number and effects of unmatched entries are unspecified.",
        "7.1.7; 10.4; 11.2=1 — Described drawings with scale bars all comply with the rule, allowing an always-yes strategy to obtain yes/no credit on that portion. This documents a design vulnerability, not use of the strategy by a tested AI.",
        "9.7 — In the 16-question performance group, one additional correct answer changes accuracy by 6.25 percentage points. This establishes coarse score resolution, not a standard error or confidence interval.",
        "6.3.8=1 — Exact historical software, settings and inputs are not fully linked to each published result; the available package does not support complete reproduction of every result.",
        "8.3.2.1 — Revisions are identifiable through code history, but their score effects lack a clear change record. Comparability across versions is therefore unresolved.",
        "11.1.2; 6.3.7 — Public questions and rulebook create possible exposure concerns. No protected set, systematic overlap check or clear training/repeated-submission rules were established in the reviewed materials; contamination is not demonstrated."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "2.7 — Under an AI-interface reinterpretation, text comprehension, language fluency, reading, output writing and drawing/image perception are required in some tasks, but capability limits and accommodations have 'information missing'. Other prerequisite: information retrieval may be part of the evaluated configuration; its required specification is incomplete.",
        "2.14 — Preparation, administration, scoring, analysis and feedback times are unspecified. Scoring is automated, so manual calculation time is zero; elapsed computation and operator handling time remain unknown.",
        "4.1 — Availability and number of digitally generated interpretive reports are unknown. 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 4.9, 4.10 — Report identity, presentation, structure, context sensitivity, development, modifiability, transparency, content and recipients are unspecified. Paper results and software scores do not themselves establish an interpretive report system.",
        "5.3 — No licence file or complete responsible-reuse rules were found in the inspected materials; this does not establish that permission is unavailable elsewhere or reuse is prohibited.",
        "6.1.2=0 — No sufficient empirical research synthesis establishes the intended engineering-understanding construct.",
        "6.1.5 — Psychometric framework unspecified; no sufficient item difficulty/discrimination, item-total, IRT or DIF indices are supplied. 6.1.6=0; 6.1.7=0 — Scoring examples and aggregate results are not sufficient psychometric item-analysis methods or findings.",
        "6.2.6=0; 6.2.8=0; 6.2.9=0 — Precision, internal-structure and external-variable validation documentation is insufficient.",
        "6.2.11=2; 6.3.6=2 — The authors discuss information supply, wording, formatting and component familiarity, providing basic comparability guidance; systematic subgroup fairness analyses are absent.",
        "6.2.12=0; 6.3.5=0; 6.3.7=0 — Interpretive-report documentation, stakeholder-feedback instructions and sufficient eligibility/reuse restrictions are not supplied.",
        "7.1.1=0; 7.1.5=0 — Small marking-test files do not establish operational robustness or administrator/model interface quality.",
        "8.1; 8.1.1=0; 8.1.2=0; 8.1.3; 8.1.3.1=0; 8.1.3.2=0; 8.1.3.3=0; 8.1.4 — For population-relative interpretations, no relevant AI norms, representative sample, classical/continuous norming study, modelling evidence or sampling procedure is supplied. Question counts are not norm-sample sizes; norming-method applicability is unresolved.",
        "8.2; 8.2.1; 8.2.1.1=0; 8.2.1.2=0; 8.2.1.3; 8.2.1.4; 8.2.1.5=0; 8.2.2=0 — For competence-threshold interpretations, no standard-setting judges, training, judge count, procedure, agreement method/coefficient or empirical cut-score study is supplied. Two additional question reviewers are not established as standard-setting judges.",
        "8.3; 8.3.1=0; 8.3.2; 8.3.2.1=0; 8.3.2.2; 8.3.2.3; 8.3.3=0 — Norm dates, adequacy checks and fairness evidence are absent for interpretations requiring norms. The narrow raw-performance exception is recorded under reinterpretations.",
        "9.1 — No sufficient reliability coefficients or standard errors are supplied. 9.2; 9.2.1=0; 9.2.2; 9.2.3=0; 9.2.4 — Within-group internal consistency has no supplied method, sample, coefficient or sample-matching evidence; appropriateness depends on an unestablished measurement model.",
        "9.3; 9.3.1=0; 9.3.2=0; 9.3.3; 9.3.4 — No identical-condition retest study, coefficient, interval or matching information is supplied. Five different passage sets do not isolate repeatability.",
        "9.4; 9.4.1=0; 9.4.2=0; 9.4.3 — Input variants have no established alternate-form equivalence study, coefficient or sample-matching evidence.",
        "9.5; 9.5.1=0; 9.5.2; 9.5.3=0 — No IRT sample, method, indicator or precision result is supplied; use of IRT is not established.",
        "9.6; 9.6.1=0; 9.6.2; 9.6.3=0 for human answer/explanation review — Additional reviewers are described, but no sufficient comparison corpus, agreement/reliability method or coefficient is supplied. Review exceptions further limit coverage.",
        "9.7; 9.7.1=0; 9.7.2; 9.7.3=0 — One AI evaluated with five passage sets provides condition-variation evidence, but no adequate uncertainty estimate for the main comparisons. 9.8=0 — Overall score precision remains insufficiently documented.",
        "10.2; 10.2.1 — No dimensionality design is reported. 10.2.2=0; 10.2.3=0 — No factor-structure or invariance/DIF evidence establishes six distinct skills, one common skill or comparable measurement across configurations.",
        "10.3; 10.3.1; 10.3.1.2=0 — Model and random baselines do not establish theoretically justified known-group differences in engineering competence; no human-engineer baseline is reported.",
        "10.3.1.3=0; 10.3.1.4=0; 10.3.1.5=0; 10.3.1.7=0 — No sufficient convergent, discriminant, MTMM or other independent construct-relationship evidence is supplied; optional-design applicability remains unresolved.",
        "10.3.1.8=0; 10.3.1.9=0; 10.3.1.10; 10.3.1.11=0 — Relevant validation sample sizes, marker quality and study dates are insufficiently specified. The paper's 2024 date is not an exact study date; question counts do not establish a sample of independently evaluated AI systems.",
